TRPM2 in neurological disorders: A

Role of TRPM2 in neurological disorders: A. Alzheimer’s disease (AD), B. Parkinson’s disease, C. Epilepsy. A. In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), amyloid-beta (Aβ) plaque induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation that stimulates TRPM2 activation in brain tissues. TRPM2-mediated high Ca2+ influx regulates the downstream intracellular signaling pathways and molecules that trigger neuronal apoptosis, neuroinflammation, and neurovascular dysfunction, contributing to the AD pathogenesis. In neurons, TRPM2-regulated Ca2+ overload disrupts lysosomal and mitochondrial activity that induces overproduction of mitochondrial ROS and activation of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway, resulting in neuronal cell death. Simultaneously, TRPM2 mediates neuroinflammation by inducing the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-6, IL-β, leading to the activation of the glial cells (microglia and astrocytes). Additionally, TRPM2-regulated elevated Ca2+ level disrupts the endothelial cell permeability, causing neurovascular dysfunction and aiding Aβ accumulation. B. In Parkinson’s disease, TRPM2 mediates dopaminergic neuronal damage by regulating the AKT/Gsk-3β/Cas-3 apoptotic signaling axis and triggering the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Concurrently, TRPM2 triggers neuroinflammation through Ca2+ signaling that stimulates pro-inflammatory cytokine release (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-β) in glial cells (likewise AD pathogenesis). C. In epileptic seizure, TRPM2 mediates activation of the BNIP3/apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF)/endonuclease G (Endo G) signaling cascade that causes DNA fragmentation and nuclear damage, activating the caspase-independent apoptosis of neuronal cells. Additionally, it induces the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway and excessive autophagy, exacerbating the cell damage. Moreover, TRPM2 triggers neuroinflammation by activating the glial cells and modulating the AMPK/mTOR pathway to inhibit autophagy, thus preventing glial cells from transitioning towards a non-inflammatory state
